title: Buried stochastic interfaces enabling depth-multiplexed optical physical unclonable functions - Nature Communications
html:
Abstract

Physical unclonable functions (PUFs) convert irreproducible physical disorder into device-unique responses for hardware authentication. However, many optical PUFs rely on surface- or near-surface-accessible features, coupling optical readability to vulnerability to inspection, replication, and data-driven inference. Here we introduce optically hidden silicon PUFs that encode physically protected entropy at buried membrane–cavity interfaces and enable its readout through depth-selective optical gating. Annealing of high-aspect-ratio hole arrays produces multilayer silicon architectures with device-specific buried interfacial roughness concealed beneath a planarized, optically featureless surface. Spectro-angular- and polarization-selective illumination enables deterministic readout across eight buried interfaces in the primary configuration. The responses exhibit an inter-device Hamming distance of 0.5011 ± 0.0060 (mean ± s.d.), depth-plane discrimination accuracies of 98.9−99.4%, and 0.080% generated-response acceptance under a challenge-held-out best-of-Ksearch = 64 spoofing evaluation at a fixed impostor false-positive rate of 10−3. Redundancy-aware depth multiplexing yields a pairwise-redundancy-screened, spatial-predictability-adjusted effective pre-ECC response budget of ~0.74×108 bits per 200×200μm2 pattern while retaining wafer-scale manufacturability. These results establish buried-interface depth multiplexing as a scalable route to physically protected optical authentication.
